title: 12 Best Italian Beef Sandwiches in Chicago 2026 — Reddit-Backed Guide
description: The best Italian beef sandwiches in Chicago — curated from thousands of Reddit reviews. Johnnie's, Al's, Mr. Beef, Portillo's & more. Interactive map included.

faqItems.question: What is an Italian beef sandwich?
faqItems.answer: An Italian beef is a Chicago-original sandwich featuring thin-sliced, seasoned roast beef piled on a long Italian-style roll, served with the meat's cooking jus. It's typically topped with sweet peppers, hot giardiniera (a spicy pickled vegetable relish), or both. You can order it 'dry' (no extra jus), 'wet/juicy' (extra jus ladled over), or 'dipped' (the entire roll dunked in jus).

faqItems.question: What does 'dipped' mean when ordering Italian beef?
faqItems.answer: Ordering 'dipped' means the entire sandwich — bun and all — is briefly submerged in the warm beef jus before being handed to you. This saturates the bread with savory flavor but makes the sandwich extremely messy. Most purists consider dipped the proper way to eat it. 'Wet' or 'juicy' means extra jus is ladled on top without a full submersion.

faqItems.question: Should I get sweet peppers or hot peppers (giardiniera)?
faqItems.answer: Both are excellent, and many Chicagoans order 'hot and sweet' — both peppers on the same sandwich. Sweet peppers are roasted, mild, and add a mellow sweetness. Giardiniera is a spicy, oily relish of pickled vegetables (celery, peppers, olives, cauliflower) that adds crunch and heat. If you're a first-timer, try one of each or go with the combo.

faqItems.question: Where was the Italian beef sandwich invented?
faqItems.answer: The Italian beef sandwich originated in Chicago's Italian immigrant community in the 1930s. Al's #1 Italian Beef on Taylor Street claims to have invented it in 1938, while the Ferraro family behind Chef Ciccio traces their Italian beef roots to 1935. The exact origin is debated, but it's undeniably a Chicago invention born from the Italian-American community.

faqItems.question: Is Portillo's a good place to try Italian beef?
faqItems.answer: Yes — Portillo's serves a solid, consistent Italian beef sandwich and is the most accessible option for visitors. It's not considered the absolute best by Chicago purists, but it's a legitimate representation of the sandwich, widely available, and open late. Consider it a great entry point, then explore the neighborhood stands for a deeper experience.

faqItems.question: What's the difference between Italian beef at neighborhood stands vs restaurants?
faqItems.answer: Traditional Italian beef stands are no-frills operations — often cash only, with limited or no seating, where you eat standing at a counter or leaning over a trash can. The beef is the star and prices are low ($6-$10). Restaurant versions (like The Duck Inn or 3LP Chi) offer sit-down dining, premium ingredients, and creative twists, but at higher prices ($15-$20). Both are valid Chicago experiences.

faqItems.question: What's the best time to visit these Italian beef spots?
faqItems.answer: Most beef stands open for lunch and stay busy through dinner. Weekday lunchtimes (11 AM – 1 PM) at popular spots like Johnnie's and Al's can mean long lines. For shorter waits, try mid-afternoon (2-4 PM). Note that several classic spots close on Sundays, including Al's Taylor Street, Carm's, and Roma's.

places.name: Johnnie's Beef
places.address: 7500 W North Ave, Elmwood Park, IL 60707
places.whatToOrder: Italian beef dipped with sweet peppers. The sweet peppers here are legendary — crisp, bright, and the perfect counterpoint to the deeply savory jus. Add hot giardiniera if you can handle it.

redditQuotes.text: "The best Italian beef in Chicago will always spark debate, but Johnnie's comes closest to consensus. Its sandwich is considered by many to be the shining standard."
"There's a reason you'll find a line snaking around the building: Customers want the freshest beef dipped in the most savory jus and topped with the crispest, spiciest giardiniera in town."

places.insiderTip: The undisputed heavyweight champion. Johnnie's is technically in Elmwood Park, but every Chicagoan claims it. The line out the door tells you everything. Get it dipped with sweet peppers and eat standing up — there are no seats, and that's part of the charm.

places.name: Al's #1 Italian Beef
places.whatToOrder: Italian beef with hot peppers, dipped. The meat is seasoned with a secret spice blend (hints of clove and allspice) and the bright red jus is unlike any other in the city. Go to the Taylor Street original — not the outposts.

redditQuotes.text: "Al's is Italian beef royalty. The city's oldest beef stand, where the sandwich was allegedly invented in 1938."
"It's easily identifiable from the meat's nearly shredded consistency, the chopped giardiniera, and the bright red jus."

places.insiderTip: The birthplace of the Italian beef sandwich. Al's Taylor Street location is where it all started in 1938 — the nearly shredded beef, the distinctive bright red jus, and the secret spice blend have been unchanged for decades. Skip the suburban locations; the original is sacred ground.

places.name: Mr. Beef on Orleans
places.whatToOrder: Italian beef, juicy, with hot peppers. Classic and no-frills — this is the sandwich that inspired the TV show. Cash only. Eat at the communal table like the regulars do.

redditQuotes.text: "This iconic River North shop is the inspiration behind The Bear, and despite the show's popularity, still has a no-nonsense vibe and isn't filled with tourists."
"Mr. Beef is cash-only with politely impatient service, and a sparse dining room with a communal table where you can befriend someone who's been eating here for decades."

places.insiderTip: The real-life Original Beef of Chicagoland — literally the shop that inspired FX's The Bear. Despite the fame, Mr. Beef has stayed gloriously unchanged: cash only, no seats to speak of, politely impatient service, and a classic beef that needs zero gimmicks.

places.name: Jay's Beef
places.address: 4418 N Narragansett Ave, Harwood Heights, IL 60706
places.whatToOrder: Italian beef with hot peppers on Liborio Bakery bread. The freshly sliced beef and locally baked rolls set Jay's apart. The beef quality consistently wins 'best in class' in competitive rankings.

redditQuotes.text: "What started as a trailer has evolved into one of the area's iconic Italian beef stands. Northwest Siders swear by the freshly sliced beef loaded with giardiniera."
"Best Beef: Jay's. Best Gravy: Al's. Best Sweet Peppers: Johnnie's — my top 10 after ranking beef sandwiches for 5 years."

places.insiderTip: The connoisseur's pick. Jay's started as a trailer and built a cult following through sheer sandwich quality. The beef is freshly sliced (not held in jus for hours), served on rolls from nearby Liborio Bakery. Northwest Siders guard this secret fiercely.

places.name: Chef Ciccio
places.address: 600 E Grand Ave SA-16, Chicago, IL 60611
places.whatToOrder: Italian beef 'in a bath' — there's no dipped option here, just a full jus-bath with whole garlic cloves swimming in it. The beef is cut thicker than most, and the crusty rolls hold up perfectly against the soak.

redditQuotes.text: "The Ferraro family has been making Italian beef for banquets and weddings since the 1930s. Thick slices of tender beef are dunked in extremely beefy jus."
"Hiding in the most unlikely of places — the Navy Pier food court — is Chef Ciccio, a small stall with an Italian beef unlike any other."

places.insiderTip: The best-kept secret on Navy Pier. The Ferraro family has been making Italian beef since the 1930s, and their generations-old recipe produces thick-cut, impossibly tender slices dunked in a garlic-heavy jus bath. Yes, it's in a food court. No, that doesn't matter.

places.name: Tony's Italian Beef
places.whatToOrder: Italian beef with sweet peppers only — skip the giardiniera here. The perfectly spiced beef is good enough that it needs nothing else. Tony's proves that restraint can be a virtue.

redditQuotes.text: "When you're standing in line and hear 'doesn't matter, this is the best Italian beef in Chicago' from the guy behind you, it's a good sign."
"Skip the giardiniera, Tony's doesn't need it. The perfectly spiced beef topped with sweet peppers is good enough on its own, even if you order it dry."

places.insiderTip: The South Side's answer to the Italian beef question. Tony's has been doing it right for decades with a deceptively simple approach — perfectly seasoned beef, quality peppers, and no need for giardiniera. Opens at 7:30 AM for the early believers.

places.name: Carm's Beef and Italian Ice
places.whatToOrder: Italian beef dipped, plus Italian ice for dessert. The jus here is more like a peppery consommé than a cup of liquid fat — refined, flavorful, and arguably the best dipping liquid in the city.

redditQuotes.text: "Carm's is just a few blocks from Al's, sitting on a cute little corner, giving the number one spot performance anxiety. The side of jus is the best in Chicago."
"Not only is the jus the best in Chicago — more like a peppery consommé than a cup of liquid fat — but the bread is so outstanding you can even order the sandwich dry."

places.insiderTip: The scrappy underdog sitting blocks from Al's — and giving it serious competition. Carm's jus is the best in the city, period. A peppery consommé that elevates the entire sandwich. The cash-only Italian ice counter on the side is the perfect summer chaser.

places.name: Portillo's
places.whatToOrder: Italian beef, dipped, with hot peppers. Add a sausage to make it a combo. Portillo's is the gateway drug to Chicago Italian beef — accessible, consistent, and open until 1 AM. Also grab a chocolate cake shake.

redditQuotes.text: "Portillo's is the entry-level Italian beef that every tourist should try first. It's consistently good, widely available, and open late."
"Is Portillo's the best? No. Is it a damn good Italian beef at 12:30 AM when nothing else is open? Absolutely."

places.insiderTip: The chain that Chicago actually loves. Purists scoff, but Portillo's Italian beef is a legitimate entry point — consistent, accessible, and available at 1 AM. The combo (beef + Italian sausage) is the move. Is it the best? No. Is it essential Chicago eating? Absolutely.

places.name: Bob-O's Hot Dogs
places.address: 8258 W Irving Park Rd, Chicago, IL 60634
places.whatToOrder: Italian beef juicy with hot giardiniera. The beef is roasted in a garlic-heavy jus from scratch nearly daily. Named best Italian beef in 1978 by Chicago Magazine — and it's still every bit as good.

redditQuotes.text: "Don't let the name fool you — you're here for the Italian beef. Named best in town back in 1978 by Chicago Magazine — and it's still every bit as good."
"Bob-O's gets points for nostalgia, points for a patio, points for spicy beef, points for crunchy giardiniera, points for bread that holds up when you order juicy."

places.insiderTip: Don't let the name fool you — Bob-O's is an Italian beef shop that happens to also sell hot dogs. Operating since 1950, this cash-only stand roasts its beef from scratch daily in garlic-heavy jus. The patio seating is a rare luxury in the beef stand world.

places.name: Buona
places.whatToOrder: Italian beef 'baptized' (Buona's term for dipped). The slices are impossibly thin and packed with peppery flavor. The bread holds up remarkably well even fully soaked.

redditQuotes.text: "The team at Buona made some sort of Faustian bargain to achieve beef slices so thin they're beyond the scope of what's humanly possible."
"Each individual slice is packed with meaty flavor and a pleasant black peppery-ness. If you decide to get it 'baptized' — Buona's term of choice — the bread will hold up well."

places.insiderTip: Buona's secret weapon is the impossibly thin-sliced beef — paper-thin yet packed with black pepper flavor. They call dipping 'baptizing,' and the bread is engineered to survive the sacrament. Multiple locations across Chicagoland, but the Streeterville spot puts you downtown.

places.name: The Duck Inn
places.whatToOrder: The 'Decent Beef' sandwich — prime rib thinly sliced, jus flavored with Calabrian chilies, garlic, oregano, basil, and rosemary on a crusty Italian sub roll. Add black truffle shavings if you want to go full fancy.

redditQuotes.text: "With its tender meat, intoxicatingly aromatic jus, and sturdy bun, Kevin Hickey's cheffed-up offering hits all the high notes of a classic Italian beef sandwich."
"Chef-owner Kevin Hickey delivers a Decent Beef sandwich with prime rib and beefy jus flavored with Calabrian chilies. Add black truffle shavings for full decadence."

places.insiderTip: The fine-dining Italian beef for people who want white tablecloths with their jus. Chef Kevin Hickey's 'Decent Beef' uses prime rib and Calabrian chile-infused jus — and you can add truffle shavings. Is it traditional? No. Is it incredible? Absolutely. The Bridgeport gastropub setting is a vibe.

places.name: Roma's Italian Beef & Sausage
places.whatToOrder: Italian beef dipped with hot peppers. The bread-to-beef ratio is perfected after 55 years of practice — a sturdy exterior that handles the dip while staying secretly tender inside.

redditQuotes.text: "Roma's has been around for 55 years, and they've used that time to develop a bread-to-beef proportion that rivals the golden ratio of the Parthenon."
"In Chicago proper, my favorites are probably Wolfy's, Roma's... the best Italian beef sandwich in Chicago and thus the world."

places.insiderTip: Fifty-five years of perfecting the bread-to-beef ratio has paid off. Roma's is the north side neighborhood pick — no flash, no fame, just a family operation that's been quietly nailing the fundamentals since the late '60s. The dipped sandwich holds together beautifully.
